thread:
Sam (CS): heads up — Aurelia Health just finished Okta SSO signup but they can't find their API credentials in the console. They report 403 when hitting our API with the token they received via email.

Lee (Support): looking. do we have the signup claim id or the console audit?

Sam (CS): claim id in the audit log: claim-0a9f3b2. Console shows a key created event at 2026-02-18T14:22Z but under `project: partner-internal-248` not their org.

Provisioner Bot: automated log -> claim-0a9f3b2 processed by provisioner v2.3.1. created credential: cred-a7f6. attempted bind -> WARN: service account creation blocked by org policy restrictedServiceAcctCreation. bind_status=FAILED

Maria (Onboarding): ok that's consistent. the provisioner created the credential but the binding failed and it fell back into the default partner project. That explains the 403 since the key is not in Aurelia's project.

Lee (Support): can you paste the curl the customer ran and the exact 403 text? we should confirm it's the project mismatch error.

Sam (CS): customer curl: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <cred-a7f6>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'` response: `{"error":"403 Forbidden","message":"access to project 'aurelia-prod' denied for credential"}`

Jordan (SRE): that message is from our tenant gate. root cause looks like org policy on their org prevented service account creation during bind. provisioner didn't surface the failure clearly, so it left the cred attached to fallback project. we need a manual rebind and a provisioner fix.

Maria (Onboarding): steps to remediate now: 1) create a service role in Aurelia's project and link the credential manually, or 2) temporarily relax org policy and re-run provisioner with claim override. which is acceptable?

Sam (CS): Aurelia prefers we don't touch their org policies. they asked for us to rebind on our side if possible.

Lee (Support): I can perform a manual rebind if SRE approves creating a service identity inside Aurelia's project via our org-admin role. Jordan?

Jordan (SRE): I can do a one-off: create service identity `svc-redwood-provision-aurelia` in Aurelia's project, then bind cred-a7f6 to that service identity. I'll also add an allowlist entry so future claims don't hit the org policy gate. doing now, will post command and logs.

Provisioner Bot: manual action recorded -> admin-bind cred-a7f6 -> project aurelia-prod by user jordan.sre.

Jordan (SRE): ran: `redwood-admin bind-credential --cred cred-a7f6 --project aurelia-prod --service-id svc-redwood-provision-aurelia` returned OK; test curl now?

Sam (CS): forwarded to customer, they ran same curl and now get 200 + tokens back. customer confirms: "Working now, thanks!" :white_check_mark:

Maria (Onboarding): filing follow-up bug: provisioner should mark claim as BIND_FAILED and surface org-policy reason in UI + webhook. also add retry path that requests admin approval if org policy blocks service creation.

Lee (Support): creating ticket INF-5238 for follow-up automation and to avoid manual SRE touch for future customers. assigning to eng-onboard + eng-sre.

Sam (CS): I'll let Aurelia know the short term fix and we can offer docs for customers who lock down service account creation. thanks team. :pray:
summary: Aurelia Health Okta SSO signup created credential but binding failed due to customer's org policy; credential landed in partner project -> 403. manual admin bind performed; follow-up bug and ticket created.
